concepts.name: Alphabet
concepts.summary: A script with a small set of signs that each stand for a single consonant or vowel, so that any word can be spelled from a few dozen letters.

concepts.name: Universal character encoding
concepts.summary: One agreed numbering of the characters of all the world's scripts, so that any text can be stored, sent and shown by any computer.

concepts.name: Tally
concepts.summary: Keeping count by making one lasting mark for each thing counted.

concepts.name: Token accounting
concepts.summary: Keeping track of goods and debts with small counters, each standing for a fixed amount of one commodity.

concepts.name: Library
concepts.summary: A lasting collection of written works gathered from many sources, arranged and listed so that readers can find what it holds.

concepts.name: Codex
concepts.summary: A book of folded leaves bound along one edge, written on both sides and opened at any page.

concepts.name: Knotted-cord records
concepts.summary: Recording numbers and other information in the knots, colours and arrangement of cords.

concepts.name: Mnemonic record objects
concepts.summary: Made objects whose patterns or marks let trained keepers and messengers recall and prove agreements, histories and messages.

concepts.name: Open collaborative reference work
concepts.summary: A reference work that anyone may edit over a network, kept reliable by open revision history and community rules.

concepts.name: Woodblock printing
concepts.summary: Printing many copies of a page of text or pictures from one carved wooden block.

concepts.name: Newspaper
concepts.summary: A dated printed publication of current news, issued to the public at regular short intervals.

concepts.name: Drum speech signalling
concepts.summary: Sending worded messages over long distances with drums or slit gongs that copy the tones and rhythms of speech.

concepts.name: Uniform prepaid post
concepts.summary: A public letter service charging one low price by weight regardless of distance, paid in advance by the sender.

concepts.name: Optical telegraph
concepts.summary: A permanent chain of signalling stations within sight of each other that passes coded messages far faster than a rider.

concepts.name: Telephone
concepts.summary: Sending live speech over a distance as a varying electric current.

concepts.name: Information theory
concepts.summary: A mathematical measure of information and proof of how much can be sent reliably through a noisy channel.

concepts.name: Cellular mobile telephony
concepts.summary: A telephone network of many small radio cells that reuses frequencies and hands calls from cell to cell, so that very large numbers of people can call while moving.

concepts.name: Radio broadcasting
concepts.summary: Sending speech and music by radio on a regular schedule to anyone with a receiver.

concepts.name: Television broadcasting
concepts.summary: Sending moving pictures with sound by radio to receivers in homes, using electronic cameras and displays.

concepts.name: Photography
concepts.summary: Making a lasting image by the action of light on a sensitive surface.

concepts.name: Sound recording
concepts.summary: Capturing sound in a lasting form from which it can be played back.

concepts.name: Motion pictures
concepts.summary: Photographing movement as a rapid series of images on a strip of film and showing them so that the movement is seen again.

concepts.name: Thermionic valve
concepts.summary: A sealed tube in which a heated cathode gives off electrons whose flow a small voltage can switch or amplify.

concepts.name: Blue and white light-emitting diodes
concepts.summary: Semiconductor diodes that emit bright blue light efficiently, which with a phosphor or with red and green diodes gives white light.

concepts.name: General-purpose computing on graphics processors
concepts.summary: Using the many simple processors of a graphics chip to run ordinary numerical programs in parallel.

concepts.name: Punched-card data processing
concepts.summary: Recording each item of data as holes in a card so that machines can count, sort and add the records.

concepts.name: Programmable digital computer
concepts.summary: A machine that automatically carries out any sequence of arithmetic and logical steps given to it as a program.

concepts.name: Personal computer
concepts.summary: A complete general-purpose computer cheap and small enough to be owned and used by one person.

concepts.name: Graphical user interface
concepts.summary: Working a computer by pointing at pictures, windows and menus on a screen instead of typing commands.

concepts.name: Smartphone
concepts.summary: A pocket computer with a touch screen, a telephone, sensors and constant network access that runs programs of the owner's choosing.

concepts.name: Flash memory
concepts.summary: A chip that keeps data without power and can be erased and rewritten electrically in blocks.

concepts.name: Portable operating system
concepts.summary: An operating system written in a high-level language, so that the same system and its programs can be moved to many kinds of computer.

concepts.name: Relational database
concepts.summary: Keeping data as tables of rows that are related by shared values and queried by stating what is wanted, not how to find it.

concepts.name: Open-source software
concepts.summary: Software whose source text anyone may use, change and share, developed in the open by people who need not belong to one organisation.

concepts.name: Packet switching
concepts.summary: Sending data as small separately addressed blocks that find their own way through a shared network and are reassembled on arrival.

concepts.name: Internetworking
concepts.summary: Joining separate computer networks of different kinds into one, with a common protocol that carries data across all of them.

concepts.name: Web search engine
concepts.summary: A service that indexes the text of the public web automatically and returns ranked pages for any query.

concepts.name: Wireless local-area network
concepts.summary: Linking computers to each other and to the internet at high speed by short-range radio in unlicensed bands.

concepts.name: Social networking service
concepts.summary: An online service where each person keeps a profile, links to others they know, and shares writing and pictures with those links.

concepts.name: Cloud computing
concepts.summary: Renting computing power and storage over the internet by the hour, in any amount, from very large shared data centres.

concepts.name: Trainable artificial neural network
concepts.summary: A network of simple connected units that learns a task by adjusting the strengths of its connections from examples.

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.summary: Training a many-layered network by passing its output error backwards through the layers to work out how each connection should change.

concepts.name: Deep learning at scale
concepts.summary: Training very large many-layered networks on large data sets with fast parallel hardware, so that they learn their own features and outperform hand-designed methods.

concepts.name: Transformer model
concepts.summary: A neural network built on attention, which relates every part of its input to every other part at once and so can be trained on very large data in parallel.

concepts.name: General-purpose language model
concepts.summary: A single very large model trained on text that can carry out many language tasks from a plain instruction, without being built for each one.
